Bill.BriefDescription: Providing a state property tax rebate.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing a state property tax rebate; adding anew section to chapter 84.69 RCW; and declaring an emergency.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 84.69 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText:
(1) The department of revenue shall within twenty days of theeffective date of this act issue a refund check to all eligible realproperty owners who paid state property taxes in 2007. The refund isequal to four hundred dollars for each eligible real property owner.The department may use information from the tax rolls of each county toidentify all eligible real property owners under this section. Anysuch refunds shall be made by means of vouchers approved by thedepartment and by the issuance of state warrants drawn upon and payablefrom such funds as the legislature may provide. (2)(a) For the purposes of this section, "eligible real propertyowner" means a person who paid state property taxes imposed upon aresidence owned and occupied by the person as a principal place ofresidence in calendar year 2007. p. 1 HB 2419 (b) For the purposes of this section, the terms "residence,""owned," and "occupied" have meanings consistent with their meanings inRCW 84.36.379 through 84.36.389. (3) Any eligible real property owner may return the state propertytax rebate check to the department indicating that the owner wishes tohave the rebate check spent on any of the following state governmentservices:
Education□
Health Care□
Parks□
Transportation□
General Fund□ The department shall keep a record of all rebate checks returnedand prepare a report to the appropriate committees of the legislatureby November 1, 2008, indicating the total number of rebate checksreturned, the total amount of rebates returned, and which stategovernment services were checked on the returned rebate check. Thedepartment shall credit all returned rebate checks to the appropriatefund.
This act is necessary for the immediatepreservation of the public peace, health, or safety, or support of thestate government and its existing public institutions, and takes effectimmediately.
